To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the hierarchical approach allows us to account for more variability and uncertainty into SSD, (ii) it is able to estimate the global response of a community of species, (iii) it highlights a wide variability within a set of species for all the concentration-effect model parameters and a potential correlation among them and (iv) it shows that the uncertainty of the estimated sensitivity increases with the effect level.

the species sensitivity distribution (SDS) can be used to estimate a global response of a community to a contaminant and that it should not be built on an effect lower than the 50% of the maximum response.

the hierarchical modelling of species sensitivity distributions is a useful tool to account for more variability and uncertainty into ecotoxicological risk assessment and to assess the global response of a community to a contaminant.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new methodological framework for the construction of an SSD, which takes into account all the sources of variability and allows the computation of a global response for a community of organisms.
the development of a new approach to build SSD, accounting for more sources of variation and uncertainty, and to estimate a global response of a community to a contaminant.
improving the current SSD approach and provides a better understanding of the ecotoxicological risk of contaminants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 95% protection level of the community would be achieved by keeping the concentration of the six studied herbicides below 10-15 μg/L. The methodology developed in
the herbicide concentration that protects 95% of species would preserve about 80-86%, but not more than 90%, of the global response of diatoms.
, to assess a risk to biodiversity, a SSD should be based on the most reliable data and the uncertainty on the sensitivity should be taken into account.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SSD approach is an interesting tool to assess the risk of a community, but it should be improved by considering the variability of the parameters of the models and the uncertainty in the estimated sensitivities.
the SSD is not a good indicator of the risk for a community, but it is a good indicator of a risk for the species.
the hierarchical model is a powerful and flexible tool to assess the risk of contaminants to the biodiversity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a more complete and realistic model of the toxicity of contaminants to species should be built, in order to better predict the risk for biodiversity.
the current SSD approach should be revised to take into account all the sources of uncertainty and variability.

, in addition to the traditional SSD approach, we provide a new way to assess the risk to a community of species exposed to a chemical contaminant, which is based on a global response of a community to the chemical.
